connection_condition: each comment record carries the identifier of the single post it annotates
description: A post is composed of its comments; a comment has no meaning without the post it annotates.

connection_condition: each vote record carries the identifier of the post it was cast on
description: A post accumulates the votes cast on it; a vote record is a component of the post's standing history.

connection_condition: each revision record carries the identifier of the post it belongs to
description: A post is composed of its revision records; revision records document the life of one post and are meaningless without it.

connection_condition: each badge award record carries the identifier of the user who received it
description: A user account accumulates badge awards; an award record exists only as an event on one account.

connection_condition: each post carries the identifier of the account that created it
description: A user account is composed of the posts it owns; ownership attaches a post to exactly one creating account.
A question post is one subtype of post, selected by the post type enumeration; its attribute set is a subset of the post attribute set plus question-only attributes.
An answer post is one subtype of post, selected by the post type enumeration; it lacks the question-only attributes of title, tag list and view count.
A post edit is one subtype of post revision record, selected by the revision type enumeration; the creation records are not edits.

connection_condition: the delimited labels attached to a question correspond to the label text of catalogue tag entries
description: The labels attached to a post and the catalogue tag entries express the same topical concept in two physical representations, so a label found on a post can be resolved to its catalogue entry and vice versa.

connection_condition: where both are present they carry the same person name; no mismatches were observed between the copies and the account record
description: Names stored on activity records are copies of the account display name, so either representation can be used to recognise the same person.
A user's badge count is derived by counting that user's badge award records.
Influence is derived from reputation standing: the most influential user is the account holding the greatest reputation value.
A percentage share over posts is derived from the count of posts satisfying a stated condition divided by the count of posts in the reference population.
A user's first vote is derived as the earliest vote date among that user's vote records.
The first award of a named badge is derived as the earliest award timestamp among records of that badge name.

connection_condition: reached by combining the post creator with that creator's reputation value; there is no direct structural link between the two columns
description: The standing of a user and the standing of the content that user produced are business-related, so cohort questions combine the two.
Popularity and approval are distinct but related measures of the same post; a post can be highly viewed yet low scoring.
A question's headline words and its attached labels both describe the same topic, so a subject named in a question may be evidenced by either.

connection_condition: reached by combining the acting user of a revision with the comments written by that user; there is no direct column link
description: Discussion and editing are both contributions to the same post by identified users, so questions link the editors of a post to the comments on it.
Recognition awards and accumulated reputation both measure community standing and tend to co-vary.
A bounty is offered through bounty vote records, so the bounty amount is a property carried by a subset of votes rather than by the post.

connection_condition: both roles reference the user table through separate columns on the same post record
description: Creation and later editing are two distinct user roles over one post and must not be conflated when attributing a post to a person.

connection_condition: reached by combining the post creator with that creator's age; no direct column link exists
description: Age cohorts and content standing are combined in cohort questions about older participants' content.
